title: Design key management and PKI as trust operations: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Who controls the key or certificate transition, and what must a relying party validate?
focalInsight: PKI trust depends on protected issuance, an appropriate trust anchor, status, and complete relying-party validation.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Key Management
nodes.definition: Governance and protection of cryptographic key authority and use.
nodes.detail: Governance and protection of cryptographic key authority and use.
nodes.decision: Assign custody, access, separation, auditing, recovery, and compromise response.
nodes.failureExample: An application administrator exports a production private key during troubleshooting.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Key access needs separate authority and evidence.

nodes.label: Key Lifecycle
nodes.definition: Controlled states from generation and binding through use, rotation, revocation, archival, and destruction.
nodes.detail: Controlled states from generation and binding through use, rotation, revocation, archival, and destruction.
nodes.decision: Define accountable transitions and test their dependent-service effects.
nodes.failureExample: A lost key has no approved recovery or destruction record.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Each key transition needs authority and a record.

nodes.label: Public Key Infrastructure
nodes.definition: Trust system that manages issuance and reliance on identity-to-key bindings.
nodes.detail: Trust system that manages issuance and reliance on identity-to-key bindings.
nodes.decision: Use when a relying party needs managed, scalable certificate trust.
nodes.failureExample: A CA issues a certificate without adequate enrollment or authorization checks.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: PKI is operational trust, not only signed data.

nodes.label: Certificate
nodes.definition: Credential binding an identity or service to a public key under issuer policy.
nodes.detail: Credential binding an identity or service to a public key under issuer policy.
nodes.decision: Check intended identity, use, validity, chain, and status before reliance.
nodes.failureExample: A valid certificate is used for a service name it was not issued for.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A certificate must fit the intended reliance.

nodes.label: Certificate Authority
nodes.definition: Authority that issues and manages certificates under a defined trust policy.
nodes.detail: Authority that issues and manages certificates under a defined trust policy.
nodes.decision: Protect issuance, signing keys, enrollment, audit, and compromise response.
nodes.failureExample: A compromised CA signing key issues arbitrary trusted certificates.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: CA protection can determine the trust scope’s blast radius.

nodes.label: Revocation
nodes.definition: Withdrawal or suspension process for a compromised or no-longer-authorized certificate or key.
nodes.detail: Withdrawal or suspension process for a compromised or no-longer-authorized certificate or key.
nodes.decision: Use when status must change before normal expiry; plan distribution and relying-party behavior.
nodes.failureExample: A compromised certificate remains accepted until its scheduled expiration.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Revocation needs timely status propagation and validation.

nodes.label: Key Rotation
nodes.definition: Planned replacement of a key and dependent configurations or credentials.
nodes.detail: Planned replacement of a key and dependent configurations or credentials.
nodes.decision: Coordinate activation, compatibility, rollback, evidence, and old-key retirement.
nodes.failureExample: A new key is deployed but clients still depend on the retired key.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Rotate the system dependency, not only the key object.

nodes.label: Key Recovery
nodes.definition: Authorized restoration of key access or capability after loss or disruption.
nodes.detail: Authorized restoration of key access or capability after loss or disruption.
nodes.decision: Allow only with scoped authority, evidence, secure handling, and testing.
nodes.failureExample: A recovery procedure becomes an unlogged way to export private keys.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Recovery must not create an uncontrolled key-release path.

nodes.label: Hardware Security Module
nodes.definition: Dedicated hardware or service boundary for protected key operations and custody.
nodes.detail: Dedicated hardware or service boundary for protected key operations and custody.
nodes.decision: Use when key extraction resistance, controlled operations, and audit are needed.
nodes.failureExample: A private key is copied into application configuration despite an HSM.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: An HSM helps only when use and administration are also constrained.
